extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners (and practitioners) on making and responding to rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 (AIA and pre‑AIA) and on double patenting issues where patents/applications have common assignees, applicants, or inventors. Covers form paragraphs, required explanatory language, available applicant showings, and procedural/precedence notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different Inventors, Common Assignee, Same Invention (8.27.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] directed to the same invention as claim [2] of commonly assigned [3]. The issue of priority under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) and possibly pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) of this single invention must be resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO normally will not institute an interference between commonly owned cases. Applicant must amend or cancel claims so the reference and instant application do not claim the same invention, or the assignee must state which entity is the prior inventor. A terminal disclaimer has no effect for pre‑AIA priority issues. Failure to comply may result in abandonment. Examiner: include form paragraph 7.03.fti and follow bracket instructions (insert patent/application number in bracket 3; brackets 1 and 2 must be for the same invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Different Inventors, Common Assignee, Inventions Not Patentably Distinct (AIA) (8.28.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] directed to an invention not patentably distinct from claim [2] of commonly assigned [3]. Specifically, [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when commonly assigned case includes claims patentably indistinct but common ownership at or before effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 100(i) is not established. Also make appropriate 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections (form paragraphs 7.21.aia family) as appropriate. Insert reference number in bracket 3 and explain why claims are patentably indistinct in bracket 4. Include form paragraph 8.28.01.aia immediately after. Also include a nonstatutory double patenting rejection using form paragraphs 8.34–8.37. Follow Examiner Notes about prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)/103 and bracket instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different Inventors, Common Assignee, Inventions Not Patentably Distinct (pre‑AIA) (8.28.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] directed to an invention not patentably distinct from claim [2] of commonly assigned [3]. Specifically, [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when commonly assigned case includes claims patentably indistinct, but no indication they were commonly assigned at the time the invention was made (pre‑AIA priority issues). Make appropriate pre‑AIA 102(e)/103(a) rejections as needed (form paragraphs 7.21.fti family). Insert reference number in bracket 3 and explain patentable indistinctness in bracket 4. Form paragraph 8.28.01.fti must follow. Also include nonstatutory double patenting rejection using form paragraphs 8.34–8.37 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory: Showing Common Ownership or Joint Research Agreement (8.28.01.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory information on how applicant/patent owner can preclude 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections based on commonly assigned cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may provide a statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) and 37 C.F.R. 1.104(c)(4)(i) that subject matter and the claimed invention were owned by the same person (not later than the effective filing date), or a statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) and 37 C.F.R. 1.104(c)(4)(ii) that the subject matter/claimed invention were made under a joint research agreement in effect on or before the effective filing date (and disclose parties' names). Such showings will preclude a 102/103 rejection based on the commonly assigned case. Alternatively, applicant may amend/cancel claims to avoid patentably indistinct claims. Note: USPTO will not institute a derivation proceeding without a timely petition; commonly assigned status affects institution of derivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory: (pre‑AIA) Showing Common Ownership or Naming Prior Inventor (8.28.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory information applicable to pre‑AIA situations following form paragraph 8.28.fti.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee can show the patentably indistinct inventions were commonly owned at the time the claimed invention was made (pre‑AIA), or name the prior inventor of the subject matter. Such a showing will preclude rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) based on the commonly assigned application that qualifies as a reference. Alternatively, applicant may amend/cancel claims so applications/patent and application no longer claim patentably indistinct inventions. Include this form paragraph once in the action after 8.28.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a),(b) Patent/Publication, and (g) (7.15.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to reject claims where a commonly assigned case qualifies as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f), or (g) and the patentably indistinct inventions were not commonly owned at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee may show common ownership at the time of invention under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and 37 C.F.R. 1.78(g), or name the prior inventor. A showing of common ownership at time of invention precludes the pre‑AIA 103(a) rejection based on the commonly assigned application. Alternatively, applicant may amend/cancel claims. This form paragraph should follow form paragraph 8.28.fti and be used only once where applicable. Follow bracket insertion rules (insert reference numbers as required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102 (AIA) (7.15.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 (AIA). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. In bracket 1 insert claim numbers under rejection; bracket 2 insert '(a)(1)' or '(a)(2)' or both; if (a)(2) applicable, use 7.15.01.aia/7.15.02.aia/7.15.03.aia where appropriate. In bracket 3 insert either 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' with explanation at end of paragraph; bracket 4 insert prior art relied upon. Precedence notes: must be preceded appropriately by 7.07/7.08/7.12.aia or 7.103. For claims claiming priority to pre‑AIA filings insert form paragraph 7.06 beforehand. If pre‑AIA 102(e) applied, follow with 7.15.01.aia/7.15.02.aia as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (7.15.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with appropriate paragraphs (7.07.fti etc.) or 7.103. In bracket 2 insert appropriate pre‑AIA paragraph letter(s). Bracket 3 insert 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' with explanation; bracket 4 insert prior art. If pre‑AIA 102(e) applied, follow with 7.15.01.fti/7.15.02.fti/7.15.03.fti. For applications with actual filing date on/after March 16, 2013 claiming priority to pre‑AIA filings, precede with 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) — Applicant Not the Inventor (7.19.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) because the applicant did not invent the claimed subject matter. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.07.fti and 7.13.fti or by 7.103. In bracket 2, insert explanation of supporting evidence establishing applicant was not the inventor. See MPEP § 2137 for required evidence and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 103 (AIA) (7.21.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.20.aia or 7.103. An explanation of the rejection must follow (see MPEP § 2144). If the rejection is provisional based on a copending application (would be prior art under 102(a)(2) if published/patented), use 7.21.01.aia instead. Insert claim numbers in bracket 1 and prior art in bracket 2. For claims claiming priority to pre‑AIA filings, precede by 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) (7.21.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.20.fti or 7.103. An explanation must follow (see MPEP § 2144). If rejection relies on prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e), determine the reference's prior art date using pre‑AIPA rules as applicable (see 7.12.fti/7.12.01.fti notes). If a copending application has an earlier effectively filed date under 35 U.S.C. 102(d), consider making a provisional rejection based on the copending application using 7.15.01.aia or 7.21.01.aia (AIA) or the pre‑AIA counterparts. Note: a terminal disclaimer alone does not obviate 102 or 103 rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Copending Applications for Provisional Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copending application has an earlier effectively filed date under 35 U.S.C. 102(d) than the claims under examination, the examiner should consider making a provisional rejection based on the copending application under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) (using 7.15.01.aia) or under 35 U.S.C. 103 (using 7.21.01.aia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly for pre‑AIA applications use the pre‑AIA form paragraphs (7.15.01.fti, 7.21.01.fti). Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 cannot be obviated solely by filing a terminal disclaimer. Where appropriate, include provisional rejection form paragraphs and explanatory paragraphs for anticipation or obviousness over copending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — Common Assignee/Applicant/Inventor (7.15.01.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in AIA cases (filed on/after March 16, 2013) and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. The copending application would be prior art if published/patented. This provisional rejection may be overcome by: (1) a 37 C.F.R. 1.130(a) showing that subject matter was obtained directly/indirectly from the inventor/joint inventor (not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) a 1.130(b) showing of prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B); or (3) a 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) statement that subject matter and claimed invention were commonly owned or subject to assignment or a joint research agreement as of the effective filing date. Terminal disclaimers do not overcome this rejection (In re Bartfeld). Examiner notes: in bracket 3 insert 'assignee', 'applicant', or 'joint inventor'; bracket 4 provide explanation of anticipation; if claims would be obvious use 7.21.01.aia instead. Require applicant to amend/cancel identical claims (form paragraph 8.27.aia) and nonstatutory double patenting rejections where not patentably distinct (8.33 and 8.34–8.39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — Common Assignee/Applicant/Inventor (7.15.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copending application would constitute prior art if published/patented. May be overcome by showing under 37 C.F.R. 1.132 that disclosed‑but‑not‑claimed inventions were derived from this application's inventor (not 'by another'), or by a showing under 37 C.F.R. 1.131(a). Terminal disclaimers do not overcome. Examiner notes: use pre‑AIPA 102(e) rules to determine prior art date per 7.12.fti/7.12.01.fti; if claims obvious over copending application use 7.21.01.fti; insert 'assignee','applicant', or 'joint inventor' in bracket 3; provide explanation of anticipation in bracket 4 if needed. Require resolution of identical subject matter (8.30/8.32) and nonstatutory double patenting (8.33/8.34–8.39) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — Common Assignee/Applicant/Joint Inventor (7.15.02.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being [2] by [3]. The applied reference has a common [4] with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in AIA cases to reject over a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO publication with an earlier prior art date under 102(a)(2) where references have common assignee/applicant or at least one common inventor. May be overcome by: (1) 37 C.F.R. 1.130(a) showing derivation (not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) 1.130(b) showing of prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B) if same invention not being claimed; or (3) 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) statement of common ownership/assignment or joint research agreement. Examiner notes: precede with 7.03.aia and 7.12.aia; in bracket 1 insert claim numbers; in bracket 3 insert prior art relied upon; in bracket 4 insert 'assignee', 'applicant', or 'joint inventor'; terminal disclaimer issues and double patenting procedure notes apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — Common Assignee/Applicant/Inventor (7.15.02.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reject over a patent or patent application publication that is prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e). Apply pre‑AIPA/AIPA rules to determine 102(e) date per 7.12.fti/7.12.01.fti. The rejection might be overcome by 37 C.F.R. 1.132 showing of derivation or by 1.131(a) showing. Examiner notes: consider benefit claims to earlier-filed provisionals and other continuity rules in determining 102(e) date; ensure proper preceding paragraphs (7.12.fti or 7.12.01.fti); patent application publications only used if preceded by 7.12.fti; handle terminal disclaimer/nonstatutory double patenting issues and resolve priority issues under 102(g) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 103 over Copending Application (7.21.01.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in AIA cases where copending application would be prior art under 102(a)(2) if published/patented. This provisional rejection may be overcome by showings under 37 C.F.R. 1.130(a) or (b) or a 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) statement of common ownership/joint research agreement. If claimed invention is fully disclosed in copending application, use 7.15.01.aia instead. Insert claim numbers in bracket 1, application number in bracket 2, and 'assignee','applicant', or 'joint inventor' in bracket 3; provide an obviousness explanation in bracket 4. If not patentably distinct from invention claimed in copending application, also make provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection (8.33 and 8.37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) over Copending Application (7.21.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional pre‑AIA 103 rejection analogous to 7.21.01.aia for pre‑AIA cases (header present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when copending application discloses invention and would be prior art under pre‑AIA provisions; may be overcome by derivation/showing of prior public disclosure or appropriate statutory statements under pre‑AIA rules. Follow corresponding pre‑AIA procedural and date‑determination rules. Insert required bracketed information and include supporting explanation of obviousness as per MPEP § 2144. If claimed invention fully disclosed in copending application, use the appropriate 102 provisional form paragraph instead.
